title: Topology-Preserving Neural Operator Learning via Hodge Decomposition
claim: Fields live on a topology-aware base complex lifted into a geometric fiber, so conserved harmonic components persist without artificial sources or sinks.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, lift/project arrows and evolve arrow
description: Three-panel schematic. Panel (a) contrasts a plain graph, a tetrahedron skeleton of nodes and edges, with a higher-order simplicial complex of the same shape, where a green filled face is added. Captions read 'nodes + edges' and 'nodes + edges + faces + cells'. A legend marks blue dots as 0-forms, yellow lines as 1-forms and green faces as 2-forms. Panel (b) shows the dual representation in HSD. A blue-labeled base complex on the left connects through curved 'lift' and 'project back' arrows to an orange-labeled fiber on the right. The fiber is a tetrahedron inside a 3D cube with orange field contours and a 'high/low field value' colorbar. Panel (c) shows a blue field blob in a meshed cube, an 'evolve' arrow, and the same field spread smoothly in a second cube. The caption reads 'No artificial source / sink (e.g., mass / flux conservation)'. Blue and orange color coding runs across the figure.
caption: Schematic overview of the discrete representation used by HSD. (a) A simplicial complex augments a graph with higher-order cells, allowing differential-form fields to assign quantities to vertices, edges, faces, and volumes. (b) HSD represents each field through a topology-aware base on the complex and a geometry-aware fiber in ambient space. (c) The harmonic component captures the globally conserved part of a field with no artificial source or sink.
abstract: In this paper, we study solution operators of physical field equations on geometric meshes from a function-space perspective. We reveal that Hodge orthogonality fundamentally resolves spectral interference by isolating unlearnable topological degrees of freedom from learnable geometric dynamics, enabling an additive approximation confined to structure-preserving subspaces. Building on Hodge theory and operator splitting, we derive a principled operator-level decomposition. The result is a Hybrid Eulerian-Lagrangian architecture with an algebraic-level inductive bias we call Hodge Spectral Duality (HSD). In our framework, we use discrete differential forms to capture topology-dominated components and an orthogonal auxiliary ambient space to represent complex local dynamics. Our method achieves superior accuracy and efficiency on geometric graphs with enhanced fidelity to physical invariants. Our code is available at https://github.com/ContinuumCoder/Hodge-Spectral-Duality
